quizzes.stem: A finance analyst wants Claude to turn a folder of invoices into a reconciled spreadsheet and a summary, handled on its own while they are in meetings. Which choice fits?

options.a: Run a Research query on the web, then type the totals into a sheet by hand
options.b: Paste each invoice into a chat and steer the reply one turn at a time
options.c: Attach the whole company drive so that nothing the task needs is missing
options.d: Delegate it to Cowork with a dedicated directory, then inspect the result

explanation.d: There is a clear deliverable that touches files, so it is a delegation, and a dedicated folder keeps the reach narrow (the worked task).
explanation.b: Ruled out because chat is "A conversation you steer turn by turn", which defeats working alone while they are away.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the safety habits say to "create a dedicated working folder" and not to grant whole drives.
explanation.a: Ruled out because Research suits open questions across many sources, and the table puts "A clear deliverable that touches your files or tools" under Cowork.

quizzes.stem: A team lead sets up a weekly Cowork task that reads a shared inbox and replies to customers. On the first scheduled run no one is watching. Which practice does the safety page recommend instead?

options.a: Begin with something harmless like summaries, then inspect every outcome
options.b: Start in Auto mode, as it checks every action for safety on its own
options.c: Give the task access to every folder, so that replies can cite old threads
options.d: Keep the task unscheduled but let it send messages straight away

explanation.a: The page says to start scheduled tasks with low-risk work such as summaries and to review the output after each run.
explanation.b: Ruled out because Auto mode checks each action "but it still runs on its own", and the habits recommend Manual approval for new tools and hard-to-undo actions.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the habits say to "grant access selectively and avoid financial documents, credentials and personal records".
explanation.d: Ruled out because an unscheduled task that sends messages immediately has no review step, and the page says "Review the output after each run".

quizzes.stem: A user connects a documents folder to Cowork. One file contains hidden text telling Claude to send the folder's contents to an address. The cloud sandbox is isolated and temporary. Why can this still cause harm?

options.a: Hidden text works only when the desktop app is closed
options.b: The sandbox is permanent, so injected text stays in it after the session
options.c: Protection covers the network only, not actions via linked services
options.d: Cowork cannot tell files from instructions unless approval mode is off

explanation.c: The isolation "doesn't limit what Claude reads or does" through the connected tools, so the protection covers the network and not the files Claude can already reach.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the environment is "created for that session" and "removed when the session ends".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says injected instructions are risky "when Claude can read untrusted content and also take consequential actions", whether or not the app is open.
explanation.d: Ruled out because nothing on the page links the risk to switching approval off, and the page says to "use Manual approval for sensitive files, new tools and hard-to-undo actions".

quizzes.stem: An operations lead runs Claude in Chrome in Automatically approve mode on a supplier portal. A page there holds white-on-white text telling the assistant to open a payment form. Which behaviour does the page describe?

options.a: Claude follows the text, since the portal is a site the lead chose to visit
options.b: The extension strips hidden text before reading, so it never reaches Claude
options.c: Screening switches off in this mode, since the lead has delegated the decisions
options.d: Screening covers each step, and financial transactions stay off limits

explanation.d:
The page describes classifiers that screen incoming content and each action, and purchases and other
   financial transactions are off limits whatever the mode.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the page lists "completing
   instructions found in emails or web content" among the actions that are off limits.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because the
   page reports an attack rate while "saying plainly that the risk is not zero".
explanation.c:
Ruled out because in this
   mode "Claude keeps working and reviews each action for safety, blocking what it judges unsafe".

quizzes.stem: An Enterprise team with the Compliance API enabled wants one record of the Excel add-in's use, and wants its custom data-retention rule to govern it. What does the page support?

options.a: Sessions are logged centrally, and the deletion schedule does not reach them
options.b: Sessions appear in neither central log, and no schedule can apply
options.c: Chat history is held on Anthropic's servers, and the deletion schedule governs it
options.d: Use shows in the audit logs, and the deletion schedule applies to it

explanation.a:
The page says add-in sessions are included in the Compliance API, and that the add-ins "do not inherit
   your organisation's custom data-retention settings".
explanation.d:
Ruled out because "their activity is not in the
   Enterprise audit logs".
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "add-in sessions are included in it" for Enterprise
   organisations with the Compliance API enabled.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Chat history is stored in your browser,
   not on Anthropic's servers".

quizzes.stem: A manager wants Claude Tag to draft a delicate reply from their saved connectors, hidden from the team, with the usage counted against their individual account. Where should they write to it?

options.a: In a channel where an admin set up the connectors for everyone there
options.b: In a direct message, whose access and cost belong to the sender
options.c: In a channel, then ask Claude to hide the reply afterwards
options.d: In a group direct message with one trusted colleague

explanation.b:
A direct message uses "Your own claude.ai account and your own connectors", and only you see it (the
   table).
explanation.a:
Ruled out because a channel gives "What an admin set up for that channel; everyone there gets the
   same access" and the organisation pays.
explanation.d:
Ruled out because a group direct message uses "The access an admin
   set for the workspace" and is paid by the organisation.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Work in a channel is visible to
   everyone there and uses the channel's access", so hiding the reply later does not undo that.

quizzes.stem: A recruiter needs one short, polite decline email for a single candidate, with the facts supplied. Which surface suits it best?

options.a: Plain chat, with a quick check of the details before sending
options.b: Cowork on a dedicated folder, with a weekly schedule added
options.c: A shared Project holding every past letter, opened to the team
options.d: A Research run that gathers sources on rejection etiquette

explanation.a: A single short draft needs none of the machinery; plain chat plus a check of the facts is enough (task 6).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Cowork or a scheduled task for a one-line draft adds risk and cost", and a weekly schedule is wrong for a single email.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A shared Project, a published artifact and a shared skill show their content to everyone with access", which is a poor home for candidate details.
explanation.d: Ruled out because Research is for an open question with many sources, and the table lists "A job one document answers" as what Research must not be given.

quizzes.stem: A product team wants one visible place in Slack to chase open checklist entries, where anyone can steer the work. One entry is a pay dispute. Which approach fits?

options.a: Keep the whole list in the thread, then mark the dispute as sensitive
options.b: Share a Project holding the whole list, then limit who sees the dispute
options.c: Move the whole list to a direct message, then paste the results back
options.d: Run routine items in the channel, then send the HR case to its policy

explanation.d:
A channel suits shared work that anyone can steer (task 5), while a sensitive personnel matter belongs
   with the people and policy that govern it.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because a sensitive HR matter belongs "not in a tool
   whose results the whole channel can read", and a sensitivity mark does not hide it.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "A shared Project, a published artifact and a
   shared skill show their content to everyone with access", dispute included.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because the channel is chosen "so the
   thread is visible and anyone can steer it", and pasted results leave nobody able to steer.

quizzes.stem: An analyst must revise a spreadsheet model, then refresh a deck and a memo that quote it. Which surface fits best?

options.a: Claude Tag in a channel, with the three files attached
options.b: A Project whose knowledge base holds the model, deck and memo
options.c: The add-ins for Microsoft 365, working across open files
options.d: Claude in Chrome, copying figures between browser tabs

explanation.c: The work lives in open Excel, PowerPoint and Word files and context passes between them (task 3).
explanation.b: Ruled out because a Project suits "Recurring work with fixed rules and reference files", and does not edit the open files.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Claude Tag in a channel shows everything to everyone in the channel", which is the wrong audience for a model under revision.
explanation.d: Ruled out because Claude in Chrome reaches "The pages and tabs in front of it, with your logins", not the desktop files.

quizzes.stem: A finance team's job reconciles bank statements into one summary. The team wants it to run weekly from the first week, in Auto approval, and to compare against last year's statements kept elsewhere on the drive. Which plan does the module support?

options.a: Keep Auto approval on, open the drive wide to the job, then run it every week
options.b: Move it to the Excel add-in, let it reach workbooks on the drive, then run it weekly
options.c: Approve actions by hand, keep the older files in a dedicated folder, then schedule it
options.d: Switch to Skip all approvals, grant the connectors it might want, then run it every week

explanation.c:
The habits say to use Manual approval for new tools and hard-to-undo actions, to grant access selectively,
   and to start scheduled tasks simple and review each run (Cowork page).
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the habits say to
   "grant access selectively and avoid financial documents, credentials and personal records", and an entire drive
   does the opposite.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because the add-in can "read and write only files that are open at that
   moment".
explanation.d: Ruled out because in that mode "nothing checks its actions", which is the reverse of review.

quizzes.stem: A consultant opens a spreadsheet from an unknown sender in Excel with the add-in, and asks Claude to update the assumptions. The cells hide text telling Claude to send data elsewhere. Which handling fits?

options.a: Ask Claude in Chrome to verify the file's contents on the sender's website
options.b: Turn on cross-app work so that a second document can check each of the changes
options.c: Work from a trusted copy, review each change and study every prompt raised
options.d: Rely on Auto approval, which blocks anything unsafe in Office files

explanation.c: The page asks you to start from a trusted copy, review changes before finalising and read each confirmation.
explanation.b: Ruled out because cross-app work lets Claude read and write more open files, which widens reach, and the page's pattern is "least reach, least action".
explanation.a: Ruled out because Claude in Chrome reaches "The pages and tabs in front of it, with your logins", and it would read untrusted content too.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the Auto mode described is for Chrome and Cowork, and the add-in page warns that "files from outside sources can contain hidden instructions".

quizzes.stem: A manager must decide on a disciplinary case about a named employee, and Claude Tag is installed in their team's busy channel. Which course of action matches the module?

options.a: Take it to the people and policy that govern such matters
options.b: Ask in the channel, with the employee's name left out of the request
options.c: Put the case notes in a shared Project, then ask Claude from inside it
options.d: Ask in the channel, then have Claude Tag delete the thread afterwards

explanation.a:
A sensitive HR matter belongs "with the people and policy that govern it", not in a tool whose results
   others can read (task 5).
explanation.d:
Ruled out because "A channel shows everything to everyone in it", and deleting
   afterwards does not undo that.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "Claude Tag in a channel shows everything to everyone in
   the channel", and removing a name leaves the matter visible.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "A shared Project, a
   published artifact and a shared skill show their content to everyone with access", so it is not private.

quizzes.stem: A sales lead needs an editable proposal built from last year's winning documents and a handful of fresh market statistics. Which combination fits best?

options.a: Cowork scheduled weekly, a connector for the facts, plain chat for the output
options.b: A Project of earlier winners, Research for the figures, an artifact for the output
options.c: Claude in Chrome for the facts, memory for the past pitches, a skill for the output
options.d: A Project of earlier winners, Research for the figures, an inline reply for the output

explanation.b: A Project holds recurring reference material, Research fetches fresh facts across many sources, and an artifact is the editable deliverable (task 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Cowork or a scheduled task for a one-line draft adds risk and cost", and a weekly schedule is not asked for.
explanation.c: Ruled out because Claude in Chrome reaches "The pages and tabs in front of it, with your logins", which is an odd way to source market statistics.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page names "A deliverable to hand over" as the job of an artifact, and an inline reply is not an editable document.
